title: Why Leaves Change Color: The Autumn Signal

scenes.title: YELLOW AND ORANGE APPEAR
scenes.caption: As chlorophyll fades, other pigments become visible.
scenes.narration: As autumn approaches, days grow shorter and temperatures often fall. Many trees begin preparing their leaves for the season ahead.

scenes.title: CHLOROPHYLL BREAKS DOWN
scenes.caption: The green pigment is no longer replaced as quickly.
scenes.narration: Trees slow the production of chlorophyll. Existing chlorophyll breaks down, so the green color gradually disappears.

scenes.title: A SEASONAL TRANSITION
scenes.caption: The same leaf can change over several weeks.
scenes.narration: Color change is gradual. A leaf may shift from green to pale yellow, then become bright gold as its pigments are revealed.

scenes.title: AUTUMN LIGHT
scenes.caption: Sunlight shines through changing leaves.
scenes.narration: The warm glow of autumn comes from light interacting with pigments in the leaf. The colors do not simply appear overnight.

scenes.title: A FOREST OF GOLD
scenes.caption: Different trees change at different times.
scenes.narration: Species, weather, and local conditions all affect timing. That is why one hillside can show several stages of autumn at once.

scenes.title: SHORTER DAYS
scenes.caption: Day length is an important seasonal cue.
scenes.narration: The shortening day length helps many trees sense that winter is coming. It is one of the signals that starts the change.
